detailed_rationale:
Quess Corp completed a three-way demerger in June 2025, splitting its diversified conglomerate into Quess Corp (workforce/staffing management, roughly 68% of pre-demerger consolidated revenue), Digitide Solutions (BPM/Insurtech/HRO, ~14%), and Bluspring Enterprises (facilities management and industrial services, ~18%), each now separately listed. Quess Corp today is therefore a pure-play staffing and workforce-management business, India's largest, with headcount of about 482,000 (+4.5% YoY).

On a like-for-like basis the post-demerger business is performing well: Q1 FY27 (Jun-2026 quarter) consolidated revenue was Rs 4,181.7 crore, up 14.5% YoY, and net profit was Rs 81.9 crore, up 60.9% YoY, with the General Staffing segment alone contributing Rs 3,596 crore of revenue. Leverage is low (D/E 0.11x) and ROE/ROCE (10.5%/17.3%) are respectable for a people-services business, and the stock trades at a reasonable 19.8x trailing earnings.

The quant screen's 3-year composite, however, scores this a clear Sell (37.05) while the 1-year composite scores it Hold (61.41) -- a large divergence explained by the fact that the trailing 3-year revenue CAGR field reads as -3.7%. That negative number is a demerger base-effect artifact: it compares today's smaller, pure-play staffing revenue base against a 3-years-ago base that still included the now-separately-listed Digitide and Bluspring businesses, making the comparison apples-to-oranges rather than a real decline. The actual, current, like-for-like business is growing double-digits in both revenue and profit.
recommendation_rationale: The 3-year Sell score is being driven by a demerger base-effect distortion in the trailing revenue-CAGR field, not by a real business decline -- the current like-for-like staffing business is growing revenue 14.5% and profit 61% YoY with low leverage and reasonable returns. I am rescuing this to Hold on that corrected read, and flagging the underlying data issue separately since it is a methodology gap, not a stock-specific judgment call.
summary: Quess Corp recently split into three separately listed companies, and what remains under the Quess Corp name is now purely its staffing and workforce-management business -- the largest in India. On a fair, apples-to-apples basis this remaining business is growing well, with double-digit revenue growth and profit up sharply in the latest quarter. Some of the scoring data used to screen this stock understates its growth because it compares today's smaller, focused business against a historical base that included businesses since spun off; correcting for that, we view this as a hold.
positive_para: The pure-play staffing business is growing at a healthy clip on a like-for-like basis -- revenue up 14.5% and net profit up 60.9% YoY in the latest quarter -- with low leverage (D/E 0.11x) and a reasonable valuation (19.8x trailing earnings) for the country's largest workforce-management platform, covering over 480,000 associates.
negative_para: Staffing is a structurally thin-margin, people-intensive business (the General Staffing segment's EBITDA of Rs 51 crore on Rs 3,596 crore of revenue is normal for the industry but leaves little room for cost shocks or wage-inflation surprises to be absorbed), and post-demerger the company is now a single-business bet on Indian formal-sector staffing demand rather than the more diversified group it used to be. Execution risk in the newly independent Digitide and Bluspring entities (no longer part of Quess Corp's numbers) is also worth tracking as a signal of how well the demerger overall is being managed by the leadership team, even though it does not directly affect Quess Corp's own P&L.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At 19.8x trailing earnings for a staffing business growing revenue in the mid-teens with profit growing faster off margin improvement, the multiple looks reasonable rather than demanding -- this is close to a fair-value read once the demerger base-effect distortion in the trailing growth data is corrected for.
escalation_reason: The quant screen's revenue_cagr_3y and composite_3y fields for QUESS are materially distorted by the June-2025 three-way demerger (Quess Corp / Digitide Solutions / Bluspring Enterprises): comparing today's smaller, pure-play staffing revenue base against a 3-year-ago base that still included the now-separately-listed Digitide and Bluspring revenue produces a false -3.7% 'decline' when the actual like-for-like business is growing double digits. This is a methodology gap, not a QUESS-specific issue -- it will symmetrically distort the trailing-3y growth/composite scores for Digitide Solutions and Bluspring Enterprises themselves (in the opposite direction, likely overstating their growth versus a too-small historical base), and for any other recently demerged or spun-off name in the 750 universe. Recommend the quant team consider either excluding recently-demerged names from the 3y screen with a flag, or building a pro-forma-adjusted revenue base for the trailing-3y calculation.
